subject: Pilot kickoff: Medigo POC scope & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot kickoff: Medigo POC scope & next steps

Hi Elena / David —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before we start the pilot. Please correct anything I missed.

High-level pain points you described:
- Frequent false positives on clinical routing (NLP extraction inconsistent across note types)
- High per-request cost from current provider; need predictable unit economics for inference at scale
- Latency spikes during batch ingestion windows impacting downstream workflows

Goal for pilot (agreed):
- Evaluate whether Redwood inference with prefix caching + workload-aware batching reduces latency and per-token cost while maintaining entity extraction F1 >= 0.86 on your sampled prompt set.
- Prove end-to-end integration: ingest 1 week of anonymized notes, run inference, and push structured outputs to your validation pipeline.

Scope & success metrics:
- Duration: 3-week pilot (2 weeks evaluation + 1 week integration)
- Targets: median per-request latency < 180ms for 512-token requests; cost per 1k tokens <= current baseline - 30%; entity extraction F1 >= 0.86 on your labeled prompts
- Data: you provide a 5k-sample prompt set (we discussed the CSV you shared) and a 500-record validation subset with labels

Pilot components / deliverables:
1) Access & infra: Dedicated pilot pool (2x A100-equivalent gpus) in our EU tenant; network access via your S3 presigned buckets / temporary VPC peering
2) Prompt/eval run: Redwood runs the provided prompt set, returns per-prompt outputs + per-token cost breakdown
3) Quality report: precision/recall/F1 on validation subset, latency and cost telemetry
4) Actionable recommendations: batching/quantization profile and one follow-up plan to reduce cost further

Owners & initial owners:
- Redwood: Jonas Weber (sales / pilot lead), Marissa Cole (solutions engineer, evals & prompts), Monica Patel (enterprise ops, provisioning and invoices)
- Medigo: Elena Rossi (clinical lead), David Chen (platform / infra)

Access/setup steps we agreed on:
- Medigo: share S3 bucket name and a service account with read-only access to the sample CSV and validation subset
- Medigo: sign the attached POC_SOW_Medigo_v1.pdf (simple 3-week SOW) so we can provision Dedicated capacity
- Redwood: send a temporary onboarding account + invite to our evaluation console; Marissa will share prompt prep guidelines

Attachments: POC_SOW_Medigo_v1.pdf, medigo_sample_prompt_set.csv (sample format)

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Elena: share S3 access + signed SOW by end of next week (11/19) — ACTION: Elena
- Jonas: share provisioning request with infra & confirm pilot start date once SOW signed — ACTION: Jonas (by 11/20)
- Marissa: review prompt set and flag any formatting issues (by 11/14)

If this looks right I’ll queue the provisioning request and we can aim to start the pilot the week of 11/24.

Thanks — excited to partner on this.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.com

2) Cost estimate: can you provide a ballpark committed spend for the 3-week pilot so procurement can pre-approve?
3) Timeline: if we sign by 11/19, you mentioned a possible start week of 11/24 — does that assume immediate provisioning or do you need additional lead time?

Monica / Marissa — forwarding Elena's questions. TL;DR responses and asks below so we can move the provisioning + SOW.

1) Data handling: Redwood will enable encryption at rest for the Dedicated pilot and will set the retention policy to auto-delete raw inputs after 14 days unless Medigo requests otherwise. I confirmed this with Security; Marissa — can you post a one-paragraph confirmation I can send to procurement?

2) Pilot spend estimate: for a 2x A100-equivalent Dedicated pool over 3 weeks (includes 2 full evaluation runs), estimate ~EUR 6,800 (this includes reserved pilot capacity + run-time). Monica — can you create a short quote and confirm billing flow (card vs PO)? Procurement prefers a PO.

3) Provisioning lead time: once SOW signed and S3/service-account details provided, infra can provision within 48 hours. That should allow a 11/24 start if SOW signed by 11/19.

- Marissa: 1-paragraph security + retention confirmation for procurement (by EOD 11/14)
